heading.description: The slide's title, above both panes. It makes the point; the panes support it.

pane.description: Two panes, top then bottom. Each opens with `<!-- _pane: component -->` (optional; default `content`) and an optional `### title`, a short label naming what the pane holds.

whenToUse.title: Two wide components
whenToUse.body: A table, a timeline or a progress list reads across the slide. Stack two of them rather than squeezing each into half the width.

whenToUse.title: Context over evidence
whenToUse.body: A short `content` pane on top says what happened; the chart or table below shows it. Give the evidence the larger share: `rows ratio-35-65`.

antiPatterns.title: Two unrelated points
antiPatterns.body: Two panes are one argument. If the halves say different things, make two slides.

antiPatterns.title: A tall component
antiPatterns.body: A component that needs height (a `quote`, a `kpi` row, `radar`) does not read in a band; the engine re-orients or splits the slide, and `lint:deck` says so (`pane-arrange`).

antiPatterns.title: Three or more things
antiPatterns.body: A pane layout holds two panes. Three parallel items are `cards-stack` or `list`.

related.name: columns
related.when: the two components read better side by side

related.name: cards-stack
related.when: three or more parallel items, stacked

related.name: split-panel
related.when: one featured element beside supporting points

commonMistakes.fix: A `##` starts a new slide. Use `###` for a pane's title and `####` for a heading inside a pane.

commonMistakes.mistake: Naming a component in the layout's `_class` (`_class: columns bar`).
commonMistakes.fix: Each pane names its own component: `<!-- _pane: bar -->` above the pane's `###`.
